posts.title: A dry lake's high past
posts.text: Lake Woods, northern Australia's largest freshwater lake: OSL dating finds highstands about 195 and 98 ka ago, 15 to 20 m above the lake floor, but no evidence for a late MIS 3 highstand.
posts.alt: Schematic chart on an off-white (#FBFBFA) background with a forest-green accent band: lake level in metres above the lake floor against age; dated highstands at 195 ± 16 ka (20 m) and 98 ± 7 ka (15 m), a shaded window at 18.5 m for 95.9–53.8 ka, and a dashed line for the modern maximum of about 5 m.

posts.title: A 1,350-year Holocene rhythm
posts.text: An EC-Earth Holocene simulation plus 304 temperature records point to a self-sustained ~1,350-year climate oscillation, driven in the model by tropical–Antarctic ocean–atmosphere interactions.
posts.alt: Schematic cycle diagram on an off-white (#FBFBFA) background with a forest-green accent band: four boxes linked by arrows in a loop, warming with El Niño-like SST, Antarctic Bottom Water strengthens, sea-ice retreat weakens it, cooling phase; the centre reads about 1,350 years.

posts.title: No modern match for their world
posts.text: Plant-wax isotopes from Florisbad and Lombard's Drift, South Africa, with new luminescence ages: early Homo sapiens sites show contrasting plant environments with no modern analog.
posts.alt: Schematic diagram on an off-white (#FBFBFA) background with a forest-green accent band: three method boxes (luminescence ages, plant n-alkane isotopes, multiple lines of evidence) point to two partly overlapping circles, modern analogs and Middle and Late Pleistocene environments.
